gold_patch_assessment: The gold patch correctly implements the stated issue: it introduces a CommonShape enum, CommonShapes cache per Realm, and updates ~20 files to use cached shapes for closures, arguments objects, iterator results, property descriptors, error objects, string objects, regexp match arrays, and arrays. It also adds init_properties() for fast property initialization, refactors ArrayObject::new to accept ArrayCreateShape, and adds realm-specific shape initialization with GC tracing. The implementation is comprehensive and well-structured.
base_vs_gold_expectation: The verifier would REJECT the unmodified base because the test patch imports ArrayCreateShape from array_object (which doesn't exist in base code), causing a compilation failure. The verifier would ACCEPT the gold patch because the test patch's required types exist and the crate compiles. However, acceptance is based entirely on successful compilation — zero test functions actually execute.
too_narrow_risks: Zero test functions match the filter 'runtime::test_shell' — the test command runs no assertions at all, only checks compilation
No behavioral tests for arguments objects (mapped/unmapped property order, callee accessor, @@iterator)
No behavioral tests for property descriptor objects (data vs accessor, correct property names/values)
No behavioral tests for iterator result objects ({value, done} shape)
No behavioral tests for error objects with cached shapes
No behavioral tests for string wrapper objects (length property)
No behavioral tests for regexp match result arrays (index, input, groups properties)
No tests verifying realm-specificity of cached shapes
No tests verifying GC correctly traces cached shape pointers
No tests for array creation with ArrayCreateShape::Default vs Proto vs Common
A minimal stub implementation that only adds the ArrayCreateShape enum and changes array_create_in_realm's signature would pass without implementing any actual shape caching
implementation_coupling: Test patch requires ArrayCreateShape enum to exist and be importable from array_object — this is a gold-patch-specific API design choice, not a behavioral requirement
Test patch requires array_create_in_realm to accept ArrayCreateShape instead of Option<Handle<ObjectValue>> — rejects alternative implementations that keep backward-compatible signatures
Test patch requires SyntaxError::new_with_message instead of ErrorObject::new_with_message — coupled to gold patch removing ErrorObject::new_with_message(String)
Any alternative implementation that achieves shape caching but preserves the original API surface would fail the compilation check because the test patch assumes the new API
environment_risks: Test depends on Rust compilation of brimstone_core crate (~50s build time); build timeout of 3600s is adequate but build failures from unrelated dependency issues could cause false negatives
mismatches: The issue describes behavioral requirements (arguments objects must expose correct properties, arrays must reject out-of-range lengths, etc.) but the test verifies none of these — it only checks compilation
The task.toml categorizes this as 'debugging' but it is actually a performance/refactoring task (caching common shapes)

evidence.detail: Test command is 'cargo test --no-fail-fast -p brimstone_core runtime::test_shell' — the filter 'runtime::test_shell' matches zero test functions
Contains no #[test] functions or test modules — it is a runtime module, not a test module
Only modifies test_shell.rs to use ArrayCreateShape::Default and SyntaxError::new_with_message — both are API compatibility changes, not test assertions
Issue specifies detailed behavioral invariants (arguments object properties, array RangeError, property descriptors) that are not tested
Base code has array_create_in_realm(cx, realm, length, proto: Option<Handle<ObjectValue>>) — gold patch changes 4th param to ArrayCreateShape, which the test patch depends on

summary: The gold patch is a correct and comprehensive implementation of common shape caching. However, the test verifier is critically weak: the cargo test filter 'runtime::test_shell' matches zero test functions, making the entire verification a compilation-only check. The test patch is tightly coupled to the gold patch's specific API design (ArrayCreateShape enum, removed ErrorObject::new_with_message), meaning alternative correct implementations would be rejected. None of the issue's stated behavioral requirements (arguments object properties, property descriptors, iterator results, array bounds checking, realm-specificity) are actually tested. A minimal stub adding just the ArrayCreateShape enum would pass. Tests should be revised to include behavioral assertions verifying the JavaScript-visible semantics are preserved.
